title: Spectral design principles for local-excitation retention in impurity-assisted atomic arrays
summary: Enhanced local-excitation retention in atomic arrays allows to exploit cooperative radiative effects to suppress emission and prolong excited-state lifetimes. We consider an impurity-assisted setting involving a single storage atom being initially excited and study the survival of local excitation under neither write nor retrieval fields. Because the corresponding dynamics can involve multiple interfering collective modes, the survival dynamics cannot determined from the smallest collective decay rate alone.
